title: General Knowledge Studio
description: 28 original questions spanning science, history, geography, arts, and visual trivia.
author: QuizRooms

questions.prompt: Which planet in our Solar System is famous for the prominent icy ring system illustrated here?
questions.explanation: Saturn's rings are made mostly of water ice particles and rocky debris.

questions.prompt: In which European capital city would you find this world-famous wrought-iron lattice tower?
questions.explanation: The Eiffel Tower was built in Paris for the 1889 World's Fair.

questions.prompt: Which classic six-carbon aromatic hydrocarbon has the hexagonal ring structure and formula shown?
questions.explanation: Benzene (C6H6) is the foundational aromatic ring in organic chemistry.

questions.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for gold on the periodic table?
questions.explanation: Au comes from the Latin word 'aurum', meaning shining dawn.

questions.prompt: Which ocean is the largest and deepest on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean covers about one-third of Earth's surface.

questions.prompt: In what year did Apollo 11 first land humans on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed on the Moon on July 20, 1969.

questions.prompt: Which author wrote the dystopian novel '1984'?
questions.explanation: George Orwell published '1984' in 1949.

questions.prompt: How many keys are on a standard full-size acoustic piano?
questions.explanation: A standard piano has 52 white keys and 36 black keys, totaling 88.

questions.prompt: Which desert is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.explanation: The Sahara spans roughly 9.2 million square kilometers across North Africa.

questions.prompt: Which mammal is capable of true sustained flight?
questions.explanation: Bats are the only mammals capable of true powered flight; others only glide.

questions.prompt: Which Renaissance artist painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
questions.explanation: Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling between 1508 and 1512.

questions.prompt: What is the hardest naturally occurring mineral on the Mohs scale?
questions.explanation: Diamond sits at 10 on the Mohs hardness scale.

questions.prompt: Which programming language was created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991?
questions.explanation: Python was named after the comedy troupe Monty Python.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Australia?
questions.explanation: Canberra was chosen in 1908 as a compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.prompt: Which gas makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Dry air is roughly 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, and 1% argon and trace gases.

questions.prompt: Which instrument measures atmospheric pressure?
questions.explanation: Evangelista Torricelli invented the mercury barometer in 1643.

questions.prompt: In chess, which piece can only move diagonally?
questions.explanation: Each bishop stays on squares of a single color for the entire game.

questions.prompt: Which country invented the board game Go (Weiqi) over 2,500 years ago?
questions.explanation: Go originated in China and is one of the oldest continuously played board games.

questions.prompt: Which planet rotates on its side at an axial tilt of about 98 degrees?
questions.explanation: Uranus appears to roll around the Sun on its side, creating extreme 42-year seasons.

questions.prompt: What is the primary ingredient in traditional Japanese miso paste?
questions.explanation: Miso is made by fermenting soybeans with salt and koji.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through the city of Cairo?
questions.explanation: The Nile flows northward through northeastern Africa into the Mediterranean Sea.

questions.prompt: Who discovered penicillin in 1928?
questions.explanation: Fleming noticed mold inhibiting bacteria on a forgotten Petri dish.

questions.prompt: Which musical composer wrote the 'Four Seasons' violin concertos?
questions.explanation: Italian Baroque composer Antonio Vivaldi published The Four Seasons in 1725.

questions.prompt: What is the largest internal organ in the human body?
questions.explanation: While skin is the largest overall organ, the liver is the largest internal organ.

questions.prompt: Which mountain range separates Europe from Asia?
questions.explanation: The Urals run north-to-south through western Russia.

questions.prompt: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.explanation: An octopus has two branchial hearts for its gills and one systemic heart for its body.

questions.prompt: Which scientist formulated the three laws of motion and universal gravitation?
questions.explanation: Newton published Principia Mathematica in 1687.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest country in the world by land area?
questions.explanation: Vatican City covers just 0.49 square kilometers inside Rome.
